newsitem.title: UK: East Midlands, Dominion to meet - source.
newsitem.headline: East Midlands, Dominion to meet - source.

text.p: British regional electricity company East Midlands Electricity will meet its potential bidder, Dominion Resources of the U.S., for bid talks at 1700 GMT, a source close to the British company told Reuters.

The source confirmed that Dominion had agreed to meet East Midlands executives despite their insistence that they would reject any offer pitched at around 608 pence per share, which would value the electricity supplier at about 1.2 billion pounds ($1.98 billion).
Dominion Resources, a Virginia-based utility, said on November 7 that it was considering a bid "at a price not much in excess of 608 pence per share".
But East Midlands scorned the price, saying it would undervalue the Nottingham-based electricity company's prospects.
If Dominion Resources launches a takeover for East Midlands, it will be the fifth U.S. utility to bid for one of Britain's 12 cash-rich regional electricity suppliers (RECs).
Seven RECs have already been snapped up since they came up for grabs last March after the government's protective golden share expired, five years after privatisation in 1990. ($1=.6050 Pound)
